references.text: The context continues with the question of why the Lord has done this to the land, which directly follows the description of the plagues and diseases.

Solomon's prayer mentions that foreigners will come and see the destruction of the temple and the land, and ask why the Lord has done this - the same theme of foreigners bearing witness to God's judgment.
Jeremiah prophesies that many nations will pass by the city and ask why the Lord has done this to such a great city - parallel to foreigners seeing the plagues of the land.
Lamentations describes how passersby mock and shake their heads over the destruction of Jerusalem - the reaction of foreigners to God's judgment.
Earlier in Deuteronomy, the terrible plagues and diseases that the Lord will send upon the people are described - a direct parallel to 'the plagues and diseases of the land'.
Leviticus describes how the land shall be devastated so that even enemies living there will be horrified - foreigners bearing witness to the destruction.
The Lord's word about disaster over Jerusalem, which will make everyone's ears ring - parallel to the coming generation's testimony of God's judgment.
